title: Saṅkalpa for the arghya of atonement (morning)

words.meaning: for the atonement of the time that has passed

samasa.meaning: for the expiation of the lapse of time

translation.literal: For the atonement of (the proper) time having passed, I shall perform the giving of the arghya.
translation.readable: I shall offer an arghya to atone for having let the proper time pass.

meaning: The saṅkalpa, the statement of intent, for the extra arghya of atonement (prāyaścitta), offered because the proper moment may have been missed. The witness prints the opening of the saṅkalpa (mamopātta … prītyartham, ‘by way of destroying all the faults I have incurred, for the pleasure of the Supreme Lord’) once, and then only this closing part for each time of day; the opening is said before it. The verbs are first person: the worshipper speaks for himself, and the formula is the same for every performer.
in_the_rite: Morning service, step prayascitta-arghya, after a prāṇāyāma. S prints the opening of the saṅkalpa (mamopātta … prītyartham, the morning sandhyā) in parentheses before it; the text here is S’s closing part.

notes.label: traditional
notes.text: A saṅkalpa is said with the breath held after the prāṇāyāma, or immediately after it; it names the act, the time, and the purpose. The Smārta form offers the act for the pleasure of the Supreme Lord (Parameśvara); Vaiṣṇava prayogas use other wording, which is outside this edition.

notes.label: traditional
notes.text: The arghya is due at a precise moment (sunrise, midday, sunset); the extra arghya atones in case that moment was missed. M words the morning form as प्रातःसन्ध्या-कालातीत-प्रायश्चित्तार्घ्य-प्रदानं करिष्ये, the same intent (corrections.json).
